thread:
maya: heads up — we're seeing a p99 latency spike in us-west for the runtime after the 03:10 deploy. Token throughput is OK but per-request tail is spiking ~3x. KV cache miss rate jumped from 4% -> 37%.

sam: thanks — any obvious errors in logs?

maya: getting a lot of `KVCacheMiss` warnings around large prefix lookups, and GC churn on the gpu pool nodes. small snippets:```
[2026-02-14T03:12:04Z] WARN KVCacheMiss key=conv-12345 size=197kb
[2026-02-14T03:12:05Z] ERROR memmgr: eviction failed: unable to reclaim pages
```

liam: deploy-bot shows the rollout was 03:09 and included kvcache -> async eviction change (sam + maya authored). Could be regression. deploy-bot: `rollout/1776008800 completed`

sam: if the async eviction is racing with continuous batching, we could be thrashing the KV store. Suggest immediate mitigation: disable the async eviction change or pin to previous kvcache handler.

irene: also seeing node-level OOM evictions in the hotpool across AZ-a. Hotpool size has been thin for cost reasons this week (auto-scale min lowered). If we hit evacuations, latency spikes across all requests because KV lookups stall.

alex: confirmed: `hotpool-uw1-3` had 2 containers OOM and kube evict started moving pods -> cross-az network pressure. Logs: ```
Node hotpool-uw1-3 evicting 2 pods: memory pressure
Pod runtime-worker-56 -> rescheduled to uw1-b (cross-az)```

maya: plan suggestion (short): 1) immediate traffic shift of 25% from us-west to us-east until we stabilize 2) rollback async eviction patch 3) temporarily increase hotpool min nodes 4) disable batch fusion for 5m to test. Thoughts?

liam: +1 to rollback + traffic shift. For traffic shift we can use routing policy `region-prefer` and simple weights. I can push a canary route now.

sam: rollback is safest first. Oncall-bot: I will create an incident link and page infra-oncall.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-20260214-uw-spike. Paging infra-oncall.

alex: I can bump hotpool min from 4 -> 8 in the next 2min to give headroom. That will cost a bit but avoids more cross-az moves.

irene: queue: if we scale up, disable the new eviction handler simultaneously so new nodes don't get the regression.

maya: executing rollback now: `cd infra/deploy && ./rollback 1776008800`

sam: I'm disabling batch fusion on config service:```
PATCH /configs/runtime HTTP/1.1
{ "batch_fusion": false, "kvcache.async_eviction": null }
```

liam: I've started a traffic shift: `route set us-west weight=75 us-east weight=25` — monitoring.

alex: hotpool min scaled to 8. pod churn slowed. KV miss rate dropped from 37% -> 18% (preliminary).

maya: rollback helm release completed and old kvcache handler is active.

sam: after rollback, p99 went from 3x -> ~1.2x baseline within ~90s. queueing looks better.

irene: noting root cause hypothesis: async eviction change + thin hotpool -> eviction thrash -> cross-az pod moves -> kvcache misses and batch stalls. We'll need a postmortem for policy + autoscale knobs.

liam: opening a short follow-up thread for postmortem items and cost impact calc. For now I'll progressively shift 10% back every 10m if p99 holds.

maya: summary for execs: immediate rollback + hotpool scale + partial traffic shift + disable batch fusion. Impact: ~2h of elevated latency window, short routing hit to us-east.

alex: estimated extra infra cost from scaling ~ $850 for the spike period. I'll add exact numbers to the incident.

sam: next steps: create a test that reproduces eviction + kvcache async handler under load. We'll gate future rollout behind it.

maya: thanks all. keeping this thread open until we revert traffic fully and close INC-20260214-uw-spike. :thumbsup:

liam: +1 — will post final close time.

oncall-bot: incident INC-20260214-uw-spike updated: status=stabilized, responders=[maya,sam,liam,irene,alex]
